REVISED 2026-08-02, and DELIBERATELY LEFT WIDE. Two temperatures pull this parameter in opposite directions and it cannot satisfy both: N_100 at 350 C wants 2.25 (measured 1.08x target at that value), while the f_100(T) trend wants ~1.6 (the plan's own record: f_100 0.356 -> 0.824 across 300-400 C at E_a0 = 1.6). At 2.25 the modelled trend is 0.0002 -> 0.375 across the same span, against data that is roughly flat - because N_100 ~ exp(-E_a0/kT) EXACTLY (41.3x per 0.2 eV, matching 1/kT to three digits), giving a 665x swing where the data shows almost none. Narrowing to 2.25 would bake in that bad temperature dependence and HIDE the conflict, which is precisely what Tier 2/4 exist to expose. Prior widened to span both attractors; uniform rather than truncated-normal so neither end is favoured. The rev.4 range 1.45-1.85 is withdrawn: it was set with the <100> absorption channel throttled.
JUNCTION gate only, as of 2026-08-01; absorption has its own barrier (id 25)

SCREENING CANARY: was structurally inert whenever i_mobile < n_j_min_junc. If S_i^T ~ 0 after fix T0.5(c4), check n_j_min_frac reached the kernel BEFORE concluding the junction is unimportant - this parameter has already produced one false null

CALIBRATED 2026-08-02. Absorption-only success gate barrier; the parameter that unsticks <100> size. At 0.273 (gate 1.246, with psucc_abs_pref = 2.0) and E_a0_conv = 2.25, a converged I=3200 run at 350 C / 0.3 dpa gives d_100 = 7.83 nm against a 7.9 nm target (0.99x) and N_100 = 4.00e21 against 3.72e21 (1.08x), with pile = 0.0000 and delta_FP = 1.5e-08. THE LOWER BOUND IS NUMERICAL, NOT PHYSICAL: <100> has no size cap in the present model, so small dH2_abs opens the gate wide enough for unbounded growth - at 0.15 (gate 1.885) d_100 fails to converge on ANY grid tried (6.04/8.09/9.40 nm at I = 800/1600/2400, pile still 0.67 at the largest), while N_100 converges to 1.9e21 throughout. Loops that never stop growing cannot be represented at affordable cost, so the box is cut to exclude that corner; 0.26 already shows pile = 0.071 at I=3200. Restore the lower bound only after a size cap exists (loop->network, id 24). DEGENERATE with psucc_abs_pref at fixed T - only the product (the gate) is identifiable from one temperature; they separate solely through the f_100(T) spread across the three conditions, which is why psucc_abs_pref is held fixed rather than co-sampled.

TEM visibility cutoff (plan S3.1-1). DELIBERATELY NOT IN THE SALTELLI DESIGN: it is a pure post-processing transform, so two design rows differing only in d_min are the SAME simulation. Sampling it would spend 48 redundant runs (one AB column) and bury its effect inside a variance decomposition. Instead every run emits f_100_tem at all four cutoffs in 'sweep', so the sensitivity is read directly off the spread and the nuisance can be marginalised at calibration time for free. Dethloff's black-dot convention alone moves one EUROFER97 point 72% -> 45% (Appendix G.5), so this spread is a floor on sigma_model for f_100
rev.4 moved the range down; 1e-3 already saturates. Default 0 = no recovery = monotonic rho_net growth, which produced a runaway on 2026-07-31
capture width in units of b_111; run_ensemble multiplies by b_111 before writing

nominal moved 1.0 -> 5.0 (2026-08-01). At chi=1, P_ld = 0.5*(1+tanh((chi*d - (L_ld - d/2))/b_c)) is IDENTICALLY ZERO for the few-nm loops that exist: rho_net=1e14 gives L_ld=100 nm vs chi*d=6.5 nm, i.e. tanh(-315). At the EUROFER plateau rho_net~5e14 (L_ld=44.7 nm) a 7.9 nm loop needs chi~5.2 to reach P_ld=0.5. Screening w_c/chi/K_rec on a grid where P_ld==0 returns S_i=0 for all three and looks exactly like a genuine screening result - this is the T0.4b liveness prerequisite

PROMOTED FROM FIXED 2026-08-14.  T_star IS the model crossover temperature by construction -- loop_energetics._selftest asserts dF(n_ref,T*)=0 with 1/2<111> favoured below T* and <100> above -- yet it was pinned at 450 C for the whole campaign, 120 C above the measured EUROFER crossover (~330 C).  With T*=450 the driving force is negative at BOTH 300 and 350 C (-1.73 and -1.19 eV at n=50), so the only DF-gated, strongly T-dependent channel (unary) is off at both conditions and the character response is left to the kinetic Marian channels, whose T-ratios are 1.12 and 0.98-1.92. CAUTION: lowering T* alone does NOT fix the measured sizes -- dF at n=191 (3.4 nm) stays negative at both temperatures for every T* from 450 down to 100, so the sign flip is confined to loops <~2 nm.  Sample it, but do not expect it to carry the crossover on its own.

PROMOTED FROM FIXED 2026-08-14, author-directed, to bring the <100> loop cost down until 10-15 nm <100> loops are attainable.  LoopEnergetics.calibrate sets Fhat_100_0 so that dF(n_ref, T*) = 0, so n_ref DECLARES WHICH LOOP SIZE IS ENERGETICALLY NEUTRAL at the crossover temperature -- it is the <100> cost knob.  Pinned at 50 (a ~1.6 nm <100> loop) the crossover temperature rises steeply with size: 450 C at n=50 but 693 C at n=2981 (12.5 nm), so a 10-15 nm <100> loop could never be favoured at the 350 C where it is MEASURED as the dominant character.  Setting n_ref = 2982 with T* = 330 lowers Fhat_100_0 by only 22% (0.4799 -> 0.3757) and puts the flip on the measured sizes: dF at n=2981 is -5.52 eV at 300 C and +3.80 eV at 350 C.  Sizes: n = 477 (5 nm), 1908 (10 nm), 2982 (12.5 nm), 4294 (15 nm).

boundary sink spacing.  Workbook ships 1e-3 m (1 mm), which makes k2_gb=pi^2/d_g^2=9.9e6 m^-2 -- SEVEN orders below the dislocation sink, i.e. no GB channel at all.  EUROFER97 is tempered martensite: lath width 0.3-0.5 um, PAG 10-30 um.  At 4e-7 m, k2_gb=6.2e13 m^-2, comparable to Z_i*rho_d.

precipitate number density.  Workbook 1e20 m^-3 at r_p=5e-8 m is M23C6 only; EUROFER97 also carries MX (V/Ta carbonitride) at ~1e21-1e22 m^-3, r~10-20 nm, which the single-population channel cannot represent at the same time.
precipitate radius; paired with rho_p since k2_p = Z_p*rho_p*r_p.

cascade SIA cluster power-law exponent.  LOWER s_i shifts production toward LARGER clusters at fixed f_cl_i -- fewer, bigger nuclei, which is the partitioning the 2026-08-16 inventory analysis calls for.
vacancy bias at the network.  Conventionally pinned at 1.0 as the REFERENCE against which Z_i is the bias; opened here only so the net bias (Z_i-Z_v) can be probed from both sides.

precipitate bias for SIAs.  Only meaningful since the 2026-08-16 4*pi fix made Z_p a PURE bias; before that a neutral precipitate needed Z_p=12.57.  Now that k2_p=2.5e14 m^-2 dominates every other sink, this is the strongest net-bias lever in the model.
precipitate bias for vacancies; paired with Z_p_i.
lath boundary bias for SIAs.  Added 2026-08-16; 1.0 reproduces the legacy unbiased boundary exactly.
lath boundary bias for vacancies; paired with Z_gb_i.

network dislocation density.  Workbook shipped 1e13 m^-2, too low for a tempered-martensitic steel; corrected to 1e14 (EUROFER97 N+T) 2026-08-16.  Cold-worked / heavily tempered lath martensite reaches 5e14-1e15.  NOTE: conditions_S4.json sets rho_d to null so the DESIGN COLUMN controls it -- apply_theta writes the condition value AFTER the row loop, so a non-null condition would silently overwrite the design.

cascade VACANCY power-law exponent.  LOWER s_v shifts cascade vacancy production toward LARGER clusters at fixed f_cl_v -- i.e. more viable void NUCLEI rather than more monovacancies.  Added 2026-08-17 when the void deficit was re-diagnosed as nucleation-limited (density 600x low while size responds), not purely a vacancy-supply problem.
